monetization_summary.evidence: The footage shows hearts, coins, boosters, rewards, and progression locks, but no store, price, checkout, ad, or payment action.
monetization_summary.limit: This video cannot establish whether payment is required elsewhere or later in the game.

notes.title: Level 1: tightly guided onboarding
notes.gameplay: The player follows a forced match next to a box. The first board teaches one obstacle and constrains the opening move, prioritizing clarity over agency.
notes.monetization: No payment prompt is visible. The player starts with five lives and visible currencies, but their purchase routes are not shown.
notes.impression: The tutorial is readable and low-risk, although the heavy guidance delays meaningful player choice.

notes.title: Level 5: Kingdom battle
notes.gameplay: The match-3 board becomes an attack engine: matches and power-ups damage enemy structures while a move limit controls the encounter.
notes.monetization: No purchase or paid continue appears in this encounter.
notes.impression: The battle wrapper adds spectacle and a different objective without asking the player to learn a new core interaction.

notes.title: Level 8: booster introduction
notes.gameplay: The player is prompted to select the Hammer, introducing targeted board correction rather than a normal swap.
notes.monetization: The tutorial presents the Hammer as free here. The footage does not show its later price or replenishment loop.
notes.impression: This teaches the value of a scarce precision tool at a moment of low failure risk.

notes.title: Level 10: Dark Kingdom boss
notes.gameplay: The player must hit the Giant Golem before it spreads ivy. The 40-move budget supports a longer, staged fight with changing enemy pressure.
notes.monetization: No paywall or paid power-up selection is shown before the fight.
notes.impression: This is the strongest early pacing break: the enemy creates urgency and a visible reason for every match.

notes.title: Level 12: Battle Ram tutorial
notes.gameplay: The Battle Ram is introduced as a directional special action for dealing with long blocker lanes.
notes.monetization: The tutorial use is free; later acquisition cost is not visible in this source.
notes.impression: The tool is taught on a board shaped to make its purpose immediately legible.

notes.title: Level 15: returning Kingdom format
notes.gameplay: The second Kingdom level revisits combat with a more structured battlefield and a 32-move budget, reinforcing the mode after ten levels.
notes.monetization: No payment action is shown. The available boosters are visible, but ownership does not prove they were purchased.
notes.impression: Repetition at this interval turns the battle from a one-off surprise into an expected progression pillar.
